The Police Department has issued at least 124 health-order related infraction citations and 232 misdemeanor citations since March.

The County Sheriff’s Office has issued more than 500 citations for violating those health orders since the start of shelter-in-place in mid-March.

Violating health orders related to the COVID-19 pandemic is also a misdemeanor offense under California’s health code, carrying heftier penalties up to a $1,000 fine and six months in prison.
